taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO and Flora of North America. Poinsettia dentata is retained as a synonym. This species belongs to the difficult E. dentata group and should be compared directly with E. davidii.
look_here_first: If it looks like Euphorbia davidii, go straight to mature seed, capsule size, and the hairs beneath the leaves. E. dentata tends to have smaller capsules and seeds, more uniformly ovoid finely tuberculate seeds, and longer less-stiff hairs.

project_inclusion.range_basis: BONAP/NPSOT-backed county distribution locks Hays, Bexar, and Burnet; additional target-zone records occur in Edwards, Gillespie, Kerr, Kimble, Llano, Real, Schleicher, Sutton, Travis, and Uvalde.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: County PASS is based on explicit county distribution evidence, not statewide native status alone.

best_field_traits: abaxial hairs generally longer and less stiff than in E. davidii
seeds roughly 2.1–2.7 mm, rounded in cross section and evenly minute-tuberculate
one or occasionally two green cyathial glands
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Euphorbia davidii generally has larger capsules and seeds, more elliptic leaves, shorter stiffer hairs with pustular bases, and more angular irregularly lumpy seeds.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Mature seed, capsule size, and abaxial hair texture are the best separators: E. dentata has smaller, more uniformly ovoid finely tuberculate seeds and weaker filiform hairs.
